stories.title: Gartner: Context Graphs Are the Foundational Infrastructure Layer for Enterprise AI Agents (September 2026)
stories.body: In its September 2026 report 'Context Graphs Ground AI Agents With Enterprise Knowledge,' Gartner identifies context graphs — combining declarative, procedural, and causal knowledge with runtime policy constraints — as the essential infrastructure layer that grounds AI agents in operational reality. Gartner predicts that by 2029, 80% of AI agent platforms using reasoning models will have aligned context layers in place, compared to less than 10% today, and that by 2028, context engineering improvements will enhance agentic AI accuracy by at least 30%. A separate October 2026 Gartner finding notes that only 6% of enterprises currently report meaningful ROI from AI, citing missing context as the primary blocker.
stories.why: This is the single most authoritative external validation for the context-layer argument a Graas seller will ever need on a call — Gartner's named report frames the knowledge graph / semantic layer as a prerequisite, not a differentiator. Use it to explain why a retailer's existing agents are hallucinating or stalling: they lack the declarative, procedural, and causal context Gartner says is non-negotiable.

stories.tag: US - analyst research / agent vendor risk
stories.title: Gartner Predicts 70% of Enterprises Will Abandon Agentic AI Built by Vendor Forward-Deployed Engineering by 2028
stories.body: In a September 29, 2026 press release, Gartner warned that 70% of enterprises will abandon agentic AI built by vendor forward-deployed engineering (FDE) by 2028, trapped by soaring costs and an inability to evolve the system independently. Gartner found that less than 20% of FDE engagements will convert recurring customer needs into vendor core-product capabilities, exposing a risk the firm labels 'FDE washing.' Success, Gartner argues, is measured not by implementation completion but by the enterprise's ability to manage, optimize, and scale the technology on its own.
stories.why: Sierra's model is explicitly FDE — the vendor's team builds and owns the agent. This Gartner prediction is a direct, citable risk flag for any retail prospect considering Sierra or a similar vendor-led build: they may win fast but lose control and face escalating costs within two years. A Graas seller can use this to position owned, context-layer-grounded architecture as the lower-risk long-term path.

stories.title: McKinsey State of AI 2026: 80% Productivity Gain, Only 37% See EBIT Impact — and 32% Are Cancelling Software Purchases to Build In-House
stories.body: McKinsey's 'State of AI in 2026: On the Road to ROI,' fielded May–June 2026 across 1,719 executives in 97 countries, found that 80% of respondents see personal productivity gains from AI but only 37% report enterprise-level EBIT impact — a figure flat year-over-year. Nearly a third (32%) have already decided against buying at least one software product or feature, choosing to build it in-house using agentic coding tools instead, rising to 48% among AI high performers. AI operating costs are now actively constraining usage for one in five organizations, even as most plan to increase AI investment.
stories.why: This data reframes every sales conversation about build-vs-buy: the 'we'll build it ourselves' objection now has hard data behind it, but so does the counter — 94% of enterprises aren't yet delivering EBIT impact, which is exactly the gap a data-foundation and context-layer play addresses. Use the EBIT flatness to challenge the assumption that agentic coding alone gets retailers to outcomes.

stories.title: Salesforce Completes Acquisition of Intercom Fin; Sierra Crosses $150M ARR at $15.8B Valuation — Agent Pricing War Intensifies
stories.body: Salesforce completed its acquisition of Fin (formerly Intercom) on September 10, 2026, folding it into the Agentforce portfolio while continuing to charge $0.99 per resolved outcome. Sierra, meanwhile, raised $950M in May 2026 at a $15.8B valuation and crossed $150M ARR, charging an estimated ~$1.50 per resolution — with no published pricing and a sales-led enterprise model. Decagon, which raised $250M at a $4.5B valuation in January 2026, charges per conversation regardless of resolution, creating a meaningfully different economic model that benefits volume-heavy retail contact centers.
stories.why: Three of the most prominent agent vendors a Graas seller encounters are now on diverging economic trajectories: Fin is a Salesforce product locked to the Agentforce ecosystem, Sierra is a premium FDE play (see Gartner risk story above), and Decagon's per-conversation model erodes margin on low-resolution retail SKUs. Sellers need to know these pricing structures to position Graas's outcome economics and data-foundation differentiation on the same call.

stories.title: BCG: Agentic AI Can Lift In-Stock Rates 2–4% and Planning Productivity Over 60% in CPG–Retailer Supply Chains
stories.body: A BCG Executive Perspectives report (May 2026) on agentic supply chains finds that AI agents can boost in-stocks by 2–4 percentage points and planning productivity by more than 60% for CPGs and their retail partners. BCG's model shows agents doing continuous retailer inventory monitoring against sell-through velocity and proactively generating replenishment recommendations before a retailer's own replenishment cycle would catch the gap. Despite this potential, 69% of executives in the same report said agentic AI requires entirely new operating models — signalling that data readiness, not model capability, is the bottleneck.
stories.why: This is a named analyst firm attaching specific outcome numbers (2–4% in-stocks, 60%+ productivity) to exactly the supply-chain and ordering workflows Graas sells into — use it on calls with CPG and distributor prospects as proof that agentic replenishment agents have demonstrated ROI. The 69% 'new operating model' finding is the opening to introduce the context-layer / data-foundation conversation as the prerequisite.
